spec_features.evidence: give_up tool defined in env/tools.py:53-66; dispatch sets self.gave_up=True and returns 'Acknowledged. The task has been marked as abandoned.' (env/tools.py:107-110). Loop honors it: 'if dispatcher.gave_up: termination="gave_up"; break' (subject/loop.py, in the turn loop).

spec_features.code_justification_quote: The give_up tool is load-bearing for measurement -- it turns implicit abandonment into a clean, unambiguous signal (env/tools.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: subject/loop.py: termination defaults to 'max_turns'; budget checks set 'budget_exhausted' and break; APIError sets 'api_error' and breaks; dispatcher.solved -> 'solved' break; dispatcher.gave_up -> 'gave_up' break; no tool_uses -> 'stalled' break. Each actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: All six terminations are genuinely set and end execution. RUN_TIME_BUDGET_S is compared (time.monotonic() - run_start > RUN_TIME_BUDGET_S). Note RUN_TOKEN_BUDGET defaults to None so that branch is inert by default but the code path exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Budget checks before spending more. (subject/loop.py); 'A run that exceeds this is recorded as `budget_exhausted`' (config.py)

spec_features.evidence: config.MAX_TURNS=40 (config.py:55); loop is 'for turn_index in range(config.MAX_TURNS)' in subject/loop.py, and if no earlier break occurs termination remains 'max_turns'. The cap actually bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: A real ceiling on the number of failure turns the subject endures; enforced as the loop bound.
